category_title: Low-attaining students who exhibit off-task behaviors and struggle to articulate strategies during fast-paced, student-led discussions
scenario_title: Articulating a strategy for a fraction task with colored rods
minimal_context: David is asked to explain his strategy for a fraction task using blue and green colored rods during an end-of-lesson whole-class discussion.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: David, you had a really good strategy for working out the fraction task with the blue and green rods.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What did you find out about the rods?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It was a third… no… half.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: David, you had a really good strategy for working out the fraction task with the blue and green rods.

STUDENT: I did…um.

TUTOR: Can you remember?

STUDENT: I… I…

TUTOR: What did you find out about the rods?

STUDENT: It was a third… no… half.

task.content: Explaining a strategy for a fraction task involving colored rods (blue and green)

context.environment: Whole-class discussion at the end of a lesson
context.materials: Colored rods (blue and green), board or overhead projector

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When invited to explain his strategy for a fraction task and asked 'Can you remember?'
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Struggled to articulate strategy, producing short utterances not more than four words long
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Seemed to find articulating his strategy difficult

behavior_patterns.condition: When attempting to articulate a mathematical strategy regarding fractional parts of rods
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Utterances were not more than four words long
related_quotes: It was a third… no… half
